the electric field levels produced by the IEEE 802.11p system are not hazardous for automotive electronics.
the IEEE standard for inter-vehicle communication systems is not adequate to protect electronic devices against the electromagnetic interference produced by such a communication system.

(a) the electric field levels produced by a vehicle-to- vehicle system are very low and they do not exceed the maximum allowed levels by a factor higher than 10, (b) the electric field produced is not uniform inside the vehicle and it is higher in the vicinity of the vehicle’s windows.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electromagnetic immunity of automotive electronic devices to the radiation of inter-vehicle communication systems.

the characterization of the electric fields produced by the vehicle-to-vehicle system in the vicinity of a vehicle, in order to estimate the possible electromagnetic interference to the automotive electronics.

the evaluation of electromagnetic interference in the vicinity of a vehicle-to- vehicle communication system, in order to provide guidelines for the development of such systems and to assess the impact of the radiation on electronic devices.

the electric field levels generated by the inter-vehicle communication system are not hazardous for automotive electronics, and therefore, they do not represent a problem for the electromagnetic compatibility of such a system.
